description: A role privilege policy declares the minimum necessary database permissions for each service account, enforcing least-privilege, DDL separation, and PII access controls.

rules.description: Each role must declare name, type, and privileges. Role type must be one of: application, migration, analytics, admin, readonly, replication.

Only admin roles may have superuser: true, and only with a documented justification. Application, analytics, and readonly roles may never be superusers — superuser bypasses all PostgreSQL access controls.
Application and analytics roles may not have DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, or CREATE privileges. Only migration and admin roles may perform DDL operations.
No role may use ALL or ALL PRIVILEGES as a privilege grant. Every privilege must be enumerated explicitly to prevent unintended access when PostgreSQL adds new privilege types.
Any role that accesses PII-classified tables must have row_level_security: required. Without RLS, a single application bug can read all tenants' data.
At least one migration role must exist. Migration roles must have CREATE and ALTER privileges so schema migrations can run. No other role type may have these privileges.
Roles of type analytics or readonly must have SELECT only. Write privileges on analytics roles create uncontrolled data mutation vectors from reporting queries.
